introduction_markdown: Answer ALL FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. Begin each question on a new page. Give labelled diagrams where these will make the answers clearer. You are advised to read carefully through the question paper before you begin your answers. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Duration: Two hours.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following:

(i) Genotype

(ii) Homozygous

(iii) Phenotype

(iv) Heterozygous

(v) Codominance *(10 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Genotype** is the **genetic make-up** of an organism, that is the combination of **alleles** it carries for a characteristic (for example RR, Rr or rr).

(ii) **Homozygous** describes an organism (or genotype) that has **two identical alleles** of a gene (for example RR or rr), also called pure-breeding.

(iii) **Phenotype** is the **observable (physical) characteristic** of an organism, produced by its genotype and the environment (for example red pods).

(iv) **Heterozygous** describes an organism that has **two different alleles** of a gene (for example Rr), also called a hybrid.

(v) **Codominance** is the situation in which **both alleles of a heterozygous organism are fully expressed** in the phenotype, neither being dominant over the other. Example: blood group AB, where alleles $I^A$ and $I^B$ are both expressed; or roan cattle (red and white hairs).

questions.enonce_markdown:
In a certain garden of bean plants, the pod colour is either red or green. When a pure-breeding bean plant with red pods was crossed with another pure-breeding bean plant with green pods, all offspring produced red pods. When the offspring were allowed to self pollinate, the following results were obtained; 580 bean plants had red pods while 206 had green pods.

Explain the genetics of these crosses using appropriate symbols and diagrams. *(10 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Interpretation**: all the offspring (F1) of the cross between pure-breeding red and green plants are red, so **red pod colour is dominant** and green is recessive.

**Symbols**: let **R** = allele for red pods (dominant) and **r** = allele for green pods (recessive).

**Cross 1: pure-breeding red x pure-breeding green**

| | |
|---|---|
| Parents (phenotype) | Red pods x Green pods |
| Parents (genotype) | RR x rr |
| Gametes | R and R x r and r |
| F1 genotype | all **Rr** |
| F1 phenotype | all **red pods** |

**Cross 2: F1 self-pollinated (Rr x Rr)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Parents (genotype) | Rr x Rr |
| Gametes | R, r x R, r |

Punnett square:

| | **R** | **r** |
|---|---|---|
| **R** | RR (red) | Rr (red) |
| **r** | Rr (red) | rr (green) |

F2 genotypes: **1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr**. F2 phenotypes: **3 red : 1 green**.

**Comparison with the results**: the observed numbers 580 : 206 (total 786) give a ratio of about $580/206 = 2.8$, close to **3 : 1**. The expected numbers for 3 : 1 are 589.5 red and 196.5 green, very near to the observed ones. The results therefore agree with Mendel's **law of segregation**: the two alleles of a pair separate during gamete formation, and the recessive green character, hidden in the F1, reappears in one quarter of the F2.
